earlier_public_record.title: The Conformal Parametrization of Nonnegatively Curved Surfaces Is Not a Homeomorphism at Integer Smoothness
earlier_public_record.author: Alper Ferudun

comparison.assessment: Earlier Theorem1.1 includes every finite integer, both C and S², ordinary compact-open C^r and C^(r+1), the same point normalization, completeness, and the strictly positive-curvature subspace. It additionally asserts failure at every metric; the current theorem only needs constructed backgrounds.
Both use a slow spiral at r=0, compactly supported regularized logarithmic maps at positive integers, and C² curvature continuity at r>=2.

The earlier correction equals A epsilon sqrt(|z|²+delta²) plus a constant near zero, is C¹-small, and controls curvature on the annulus. The current correction is K epsilon chi sqrt(|z|²+rho²), with an exact inverse-coordinate operator and uniform fixed K. The convex-radius mechanism and full geometric conclusion already have a documented earlier antecedent.

The integrated radial correction and Brioschi remainder proof differ from the direct cutoff correction and inverse-coordinate proof. These are explicit proof differences; this review establishes no new mathematical strengthening or sufficiently novel contribution from them.

independent_proof_of_current_theorem: Supported as written; no central analytic gap identified. This is logically separate from priority.
